name: ch9_selected
title: Chapter-9.3 selected controller weights, re-confirmed on the batch network
description: Selected by constraints plus a lexicographic order on e_v(TS) with a 2 % indifference band on e_v(DS).
e_q is bounded above and reported, never minimised.
No scoring weights enter the selection.
RE-CONFIRMED 2026-09-16 on the doubled-DSO_3 batch network. The original
selection (2026-09-11) ran the whole Stage-I/II campaign on the SYMMETRIC
model, because make_config() sets no per-DSO multipliers and nothing in
Stage I or Stage II ever did -- while the Chapter-9 batch is declared on
the doubled network that the PowerFactory project stores. The campaign was
therefore re-run on the batch network and the selection rule picked the
SAME candidate, 399e30d3b60b, so these nine weights are unchanged.
What did change are the metrics the chapter quotes. Same weights,
symmetric -> batch: e_v(TS) 0.001651 -> 0.001456 (better), e_v(DS)
installed DER and active load stresses the distribution side, as expected.
The previous aggregate is retained under provenance.superseded.
The analytic screen is effectively network-invariant: over the same 512
Sobol draws both networks admit 116 survivors, per-draw lambda_max(B)
differs by a median of 0.00064, and ZERO draws change side of the 1.5459
selection ceiling. That is why the archived shortlist could be re-simulated
rather than re-screened.
shunt_int_g_w sits in the gauge-invariance group with the nine weights, so
it travels with the parameter set; leaving it in make_config at its
old-gauge value of 10 made the eight shunt banks inert for an entire
campaign. Value 0.03 derived from a 30 min persistence at the measured p90
boundary pressure |g_H| = 0.133; the independent gauge-consistent rescale
of the old value gives 0.040, so the two routes agree within 30 %.
A single very large demand may still commit within one supervisory period:
the anti-windup clamp (25 Mvar) sits above the threshold (22.5), and that
behaviour was accepted as desirable rather than designed out.
BULK SHUNT SWITCHING IS REPORTED AND NOT CONSTRAINED -- a scope decision
of 2026-09-15, recorded in tuning/stage2_search.py::Limits. At these
weights on the batch network the eight banks make 210 commits and 144
short reversals over 6 x 12 h (70 and 48 per day), with W4 -- a RANKED
window -- at 126 commits/day, against a 30 ops/day tap budget. Any use of
this selection must say that shunt wear was measured and not bounded.
